name: Apathy-Stone
geological_features: Featureless grey plains stretching to the horizon
Uniform sedimentary layers with no geological variation
description: Apathy-Stone is a rocky world of such profound geological monotony that survey teams have described it as the most boring planet in mapped space. Grey plains of uniform sedimentary rock extend in every direction, broken only by shallow depressions filled with fine grey dust. There are no mountains, no valleys, no visible craters of significance.

The thin atmosphere does nothing to enliven the landscape, carrying no weather, no wind, no variation of any kind. The sky is a permanent pale grey that blends seamlessly into the horizon, creating a featureless expanse that induces a peculiar psychological numbness in observers.

Microbial life exists in the dust, slow-metabolizing organisms so simple and so uniformly distributed that they add nothing to the planet's visual character. Geological surveys confirm that Apathy-Stone has been in this state for billions of years, its tectonic activity having ceased so long ago that erosion has worn everything to a uniform flatness.

The planet's only practical value is as a waypoint for refueling, and even this function is compromised by the documented psychological effects of prolonged exposure to its environment. Crews stationed here report a creeping indifference that persists for weeks after departure, a grey mood that mirrors the grey world, as though Apathy-Stone impresses its character upon those who visit.
